data.title: AS-REP Roasting - Accounts Without Kerberos Pre-Authentication
data.summary:
Domain accounts were configured without Kerberos pre-authentication, allowing
password material to be requested and cracked offline by an unauthenticated
attacker with no credentials of any kind.
data.description:
Kerberos pre-authentication requires a client to prove knowledge of its password
before the Key Distribution Centre will issue an authentication ticket. Where the
"Do not require Kerberos preauthentication" attribute is set on an account, this
check is skipped and the KDC will return an AS-REP message to any requester.

The returned message contains a portion encrypted with a key derived from the
account's password. An attacker requires only the account name to obtain it;
no valid domain credentials are needed, meaning this attack can be performed by
an entirely unauthenticated party with network access to a domain controller.

Because the recovered material is cracked offline, the process generates no
failed authentication events, does not increment the account lockout counter,
and remains invisible to controls that monitor authentication failures.

Accounts within the domain were identified with this attribute set. The password
of at least one such account was recovered offline using a publicly available
wordlist, indicating that the password did not meet the length required to resist
offline attack.
data.impact:
An attacker with network access to a domain controller and no credentials could
recover the plaintext password of an affected account. This provides an initial
foothold in the domain without any prior access. Where the affected account holds
elevated privileges, the attacker gains those privileges directly, and where it
holds only standard access, the account still serves as the starting point for
further attacks that require authenticated domain access.
data.recommendation:
1. Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts by clearing the
   "Do not require Kerberos preauthentication" attribute in Active Directory
   Users and Computers, or by setting the DONT_REQ_PREAUTH flag to false.

2. Where a legacy application genuinely requires the setting, document the
   business justification, restrict the account to the minimum privileges
   required, and assign it a randomly generated password of at least 25
   characters.

3. Audit the domain regularly for accounts with the attribute set, as it is
   frequently enabled during troubleshooting and never reverted.

4. Configure alerting on Kerberos event ID 4768 where the pre-authentication
   type is zero, which indicates an AS-REP request against an affected account.

5. Increase the domain minimum password length so that recovered material cannot
   be cracked within a practical timeframe.
